create.name: Kagyu Samye Dzong Edinburgh
create.bio:
Kagyu Samye Dzong Edinburgh is the Scottish capital's outpost of Samye Ling, the Dumfriesshire monastery set up in 1967, which it describes as the West's first Tibetan Buddhist centre. It belongs to the Karma Kagyu lineage, headed by the 17th Gyalwa Karmapa, Ogyen Trinley Dorje, and is guided by Lama Yeshe Losal Rinpoche, Samye Ling's abbot, and by the monastery's founder Akong Tulku Rinpoche; they appointed the senior nun Ani Rinchen Khandro to run the centre day to day. It is part of the Rokpa Trust and now has its home in Leith, with a domed shrine room and a yoga room.

The weekly programme includes guided, lunchtime and morning meditation sessions, chanting pujas such as Green Tara and Chenrezi, study groups and qigong and yoga classes, with meditation and prayer offered on a donation basis. There are also practice days, wheel days for Buddhist festivals and talks by visiting Tibetan lamas. Its recorded teaching courses, on Milarepa's songs, the Four Noble Truths, Akong Rinpoche's legacy and the Rain of Wisdom, are free to watch on its website and YouTube channel.

courses.title: Audio Teaching: The Four Preliminary Foundations – Part 1: Precious Human Life
courses.description: A downloadable recorded teaching by Ani Rinchen Khandro on the first of the four thoughts that turn the mind towards practice: the rare value of a human life.

courses.title: Audio Teaching: The Four Preliminary Foundations – Part 3: Karma, Cause and Effect
courses.description: A downloadable recorded teaching by Ani Rinchen Khandro on karma, the third of the four foundational contemplations in Tibetan Buddhism.

free_resources.title: Discovering Buddhism (online course)
free_resources.description: A free three-part recorded course with Ani Rinchen Khandro that looks at Buddhism from the Buddha's own time to how it applies in life today.

free_resources.title: The Songs of Milarepa (online course)
free_resources.description: A free series of recorded teachings on the songs of realisation of the Tibetan yogi Milarepa, read as inspiration for one's own practice.

free_resources.title: Guided Meditation sessions
free_resources.description: Drop-in meditation sessions at the Leith centre during the week, open to people of any belief and offered free, with donations welcome.

free_resources.title: Ngondro Practice Day
free_resources.description: A free practice day for people doing the Ngondro preliminary practices, opened and closed by Ani Rinchen Khandro, who also helps beginners during the day.
